title: Flagship phones are a better deal than mid-rangers in 2026, and here’s the proof
summary: Mid-range price hikes are making premium phones look like a bargain.
body: TL;DR Soaring memory and RAM prices are pushing mid-range phone prices upward, narrowing the price gap with flagship devices. Counterpoint Research reports that premium smartphones ($600+ wholesale) grabbed a record 29% of global sales in H1 2026. OEMs are aggressively offering trade-in deals, financing, and buybacks to help buyers jump to top-tier phones. The best Android phones keep creeping up in price, but this pricing squeeze is creating an unexpected silver lining for consumers: flagship smartphones are starting to look like surprisingly great deals. According to the latest H1 2026 data from Counterpoint Research , premium smartphones (wholesale prices of $600 and above) grabbed a record 29% share of total global sales — up from 25% in H1 2025. Unit sales in the segment also grew 5% year over year.

title: Google is rethinking how Quick Settings tiles behave on locked phones (again)
summary: New code indicates Google will only restrict Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Mobile Data, and Airplane Mode toggles on the lock screen.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR 1 Beta 5 code revealed Google’s plan to require unlocking to toggle all Quick Settings tiles except Flashlight. The latest Android Canary 2608 build includes code indicating a shift toward a middle ground, requiring unlocks only for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Mobile Data, and Airplane Mode toggles. The new restriction seemingly targets tiles that thieves use to disable tracking while keeping lower-risk utilities like flashlight and auto-rotate available on the lock screen. Android devices let you toggle a surprisingly large number of settings on locked devices through the Quick Settings tiles. We spotted code in Android 17 QPR 1 Beta 5 indicating Google’s intent to lock down all Quick Settings tiles except the flashlight tile , which made a lot of sense for privacy and security. However, some might find the approach too heavy-handed. Code in Android Canary 2608 indicates Google is gunning for a middle ground, with some locked Quick Settings tiles instead of almost all of them. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: Google built a portable AI translator that works offline, and you can build one too
summary: Showcasing Gemma's offline, on-device capabilities.
body: TL;DR A team of Google engineers used Gemma 4 E4B running on a Raspberry Pi 5 to build an AI translator that works offline. It comes with a touchscreen display, a push-to-talk button, and a knob to change languages. The code and 3D printing files are available on GitHub, so anyone can build their own AI translator. Google’s Gemma models are quite capable, and if you’ve been wondering exactly how good these models are, there’s something you need to see. A team of Google engineers has created a fully offline translator that uses the Gemma 4 E4B model running on a Raspberry Pi 5. The team used Google Antigravity for development and the Gemma 4 E4B model for the AI chops needed to translate different languages. They also designed a 3D-printed housing to fit all the electronics, complete with a display to show the translated text, a mic, a speaker, a push-to-talk button, and a knob to change languages.

title: OpenAI just made ChatGPT’s latest model more accessible to non-paying users
summary: Free users are getting unlimited chats and deeper thinking.
body: TL;DR OpenAI’s latest ChatGPT update brings meaningful upgrades to the GPT-5.6 lineup. The top-tier GPT-5.6 Sol model will now make fewer factual errors, limit unnecessary information, and can adapt its reasoning based on your query. Free users are moving from GPT-5.5 Instant to GPT-5.6 Luna with unlimited text chats and a new Think button for deeper reasoning. ChatGPT’s latest 5.6 model lineup made its official debut early in July. Less than a month later, the AI giant is already giving the state-of-the-art models a brain and accessibility boost. As you may recall, the 5.6 series consists of three models: Sol, Terra, and Luna. There’s no update to Terra, but GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna are getting meaningful upgrades . title: Google reveals how much free space Chrome wants to install local AI models
summary: It's kind of a lot.
body: TL;DR Google has updated its support documentation to show that downloading the models that power Chrome’s on-device AI features requires approximately 20 gigabytes of available storage space. The install size of the models is still approximately 4 GB, Google has confirmed. You can disable Chrome’s on-device AI features in the browser’s settings. Google’s been working for a while to integrate Gemini more deeply into Chrome for some time now. Some users were confused and annoyed this spring when Chrome started automatically downloading a multi-gigabyte file called weights.bin that enables Gemini Nano features to run locally. Now, Google’s updated its documentation to reflect that you’ll actually need quite a bit more free space to actually download the files required for local AI features. As spotted by Windows Report (via PiunikaWeb ), the Google Chrome Help Center entry about the browser’s on-device generative AI models has been updated to reflect that you’ll need approximately 20 gigs of free disk space to install the models that power local AI features. You’ll also need an unmetered data connection, plus “ Sufficient device performance.”

title: Reddit is letting AI decide when your post breaks the rules
summary: The machines are moving into the mod queue, and they can be given the power to delete your posts.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Reddit’s new Rules Hub uses AI to judge whether posts and comments violate the “intent” of subreddit rules. Moderators decide whether suspected violations are flagged for review or removed automatically. The optional tool is rolling out more widely later in 2026, following testing in over 700 communities. Reddit moderation has never exactly been a polished operation. It runs on volunteer moderators, user reports, and Automod rules that may have been written years ago by someone who has since vanished from the subreddit. Perhaps inevitably, AI is now also being invited behind the scenes at Reddit, with a new system that can decide whether posts and comments should be reported or removed. As The Verge reports, Reddit’s new Rules Hub uses large language models to judge whether content matches the “intent” of a subreddit rule. Automod usually looks for specific words, phrases, or patterns, while the new system is meant to understand context and handle messier cases that don’t fit neatly into a keyword filter.
